title: India Beat Wales 3-1 in Hockey World Cup Opener as Harmanpreet's Men Begin Quest to End 51-Year Title Drought
excerpt: Captain Harmanpreet Singh's squad dominated Wales in their Pool D opener at Amstelveen, scoring twice in the first quarter and never looking back.
body:
• India defeated Wales 3-1 in their FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 opener in Amstelveen, Netherlands, with goals spread across the first and third quarters
  • India took a commanding 2-0 lead in the first quarter and added a third in the third quarter before Wales managed a consolation goal in the fourth
  • Captain Harmanpreet Singh leads a 20-member squad that includes veteran Manpreet Singh, India's most-capped player, who has said this could be his final World Cup
  • India, who last won the Hockey World Cup in 1975, face England on August 17 and Pakistan on August 19 in their remaining Pool D fixtures

Dominant Start for India

India opened their FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 campaign with a commanding 3-1 victory over Wales in Amstelveen, Netherlands, on Saturday — fittingly on India's 80th Independence Day. Captain Harmanpreet Singh's squad wasted no time imposing themselves on the match, racing to a 2-0 lead in the first quarter.

https://x.com/TheHockeyIndia/status/2088574680500477995

The Indian attack was sharp and purposeful from the opening whistle, converting two of their early chances to give Wales little room to breathe. The second quarter saw both teams unable to find the net, with India content to manage their advantage and Wales struggling to create meaningful openings against a well-organized Indian defense.

Third-Quarter Cushion

India extended their lead to 3-0 in the third quarter, effectively killing the contest. The goal showcased the kind of clinical finishing that chief coach Craig Fulton has been building toward, with India's forwards linking up through quick passes and decisive entries into the circle.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Kv9b6ou1ua4

Wales pulled one back in the fourth quarter to make the final score 3-1, a result that preserved some dignity but never threatened India's control of the match. The consolation goal was the only blemish on an otherwise assured defensive display by Amit Rohidas and the Indian back line.

Manpreet's Farewell Tour

The match carried particular emotional weight for veteran midfielder Manpreet Singh, India's most-capped player in hockey history. In the lead-up to the tournament, Manpreet told ThePrint that this would "probably" be his last World Cup, adding that he was "looking to make it memorable."

Manpreet's experience in the midfield, alongside Hardik Singh and Vivek Sagar Prasad, provided the platform for India's attacking play. The 20-member squad announced by Hockey India on July 21 was described by Fulton as "the right mix of tournament experience and in-form youth who've earned their spot through performance, not reputation."

The Road Ahead in Pool D

India are drawn in Pool D alongside England, Pakistan, and Wales, with all pool-stage matches being played in Amstelveen. The schedule intensifies quickly: India face England on August 17 before the highly anticipated clash with arch-rivals Pakistan on August 19 — a fixture that consistently draws massive attention from fans across the subcontinent and the diaspora.

The victory continues India's strong recent form. In their final warm-up fixture, India demolished Pakistan 7-1 in London in the FIH Pro League, a result that sent a clear message ahead of the tournament.

Ending a 51-Year Wait

India last won the Hockey World Cup in 1975 and finished ninth in the previous edition in 2023. Fulton has built his team's tactical identity around a "press, counter, perform" philosophy, and the opening win against Wales suggests the approach is bearing fruit. Whether it can carry India deep into the knockout rounds — and potentially end a half-century title drought — will be tested against stiffer opposition in the days ahead.
